BLOCKED (response-data defect, determinate; retry test NO). data/christiannationalism_davis2021.R has an off-by-one: it sets items<-names(x)[-1] and then, looping i in 2:ncol(x), pairs data column x[,i] with label items[i] = names(x)[i+1]. So every live item code names the NEXT source column and the last column is coded with the literal string 'NA'. Source small-relig.tab (Dataverse GUSJEI fileId 5153037, CC0) column order: MOTHERLODEID, xiannation, xianvalues, pubreligion, godsplan, prayer, churchstate. Confirmed against live data (item_stats.R, n=1378 per item) by floor/ceiling counts, which match exactly: live xianvalues 40.2%/11.1% = source xiannation 554/153 of 1378; live pubreligion 29.0/14.3 = source xianvalues 400/197; live godsplan 12.4/20.7 = source pubreligion 171/285; live prayer 25.6/16.1 = source godsplan 353/222; live churchstate 16.1/28.1 = source prayer 222/387; live 'NA' 34.9/8.0 = source churchstate 481/110. The xiannation item is absent from the live table under its own name. Five of six codes are self-describing and would contradict any correctly mapped text, and the sixth is the string 'NA', which most readers coerce to missing, so the text cannot be attached to the codes without shipping a table that misleads a reader. Fix: in the processing script use items[i-1] (or names(x)[i]) and re-upload the response table; codes then become xiannation, xianvalues, pubreligion, godsplan, prayer, churchstate. After that the extraction is trivial and exempt-grade: the deposit's own xn-final-syntax.do (fileId 6317161) quotes all six items against these exact variable names, e.g. '(1) Please rate the extent to which you agree or disagree with the following statements: The federal government should declare the United States as a Christian nation. (MP12A)'; churchstate is stored reverse-coded (recode 1=5 2=4 8=3 3=2 4=1), the others as 1..5 with Undecided (BRS code 8) at 3. Would an unchanged retry right now plausibly produce a different result? NO -- only a corrected response table changes it. source_ref: Data: OSF g8dvj (https://osf.io/g8dvj/), data.csv (https://osf.io/download/6z8ht/), SurveyMonkey export; analysis script Music_Personality_Values.Rmd (https://osf.io/download/3rx5y/). Paper: Morgan, Holtzman, Hines, Dockter & Pichon (2026), J. Individual Differences 47(1):21-31. Anchors 2-6 and instructions: Rentfrow's STOMP-R form, STOMP-R.pdf linked from https://www.psd.psychol.cam.ac.uk/projects-measures (dropbox.com/s/n30bfwtgppx4z1r/STOMP-R.pdf), sha256 7ac940ed8f44007198523751d4f1ca8d5e3d9d14d9a07c841172a73a17b1b97a, fetched 2026-09-19. Processing script data/morgan_2026_music_personality.py.
note: PASS. MAPPING (data_labels, core-model pattern 1): data/morgan_2026_music_personality.py melts the raw data.csv columns STOMPR01..STOMPR23 by name and only lowercases them, so each IRW code IS the source column name; the SurveyMonkey sub-header row (row 2 of data.csv, the row the script drops) labels each column with its genre, 23/23 -- e.g. STOMPR01 'Alternative', STOMPR15 'Opera', STOMPR23 'Soundtracks/Theme Songs'. item_text is that sub-header label verbatim, which also matches the canonical STOMP-R numbering 1-23 item for item (study labels differ from the canonical form only in casing: 'Rap/Hip-Hop' vs 'Rap/hip-hop', 'Soundtracks/Theme Songs' vs 'Soundtracks/theme song'; the study's own spelling ships). Sanity: live Opera (stompr15) is the least liked genre (mean 2.52, 40.1% at 1), Country/Oldies among the most liked (4.81, 4.84) -- coherent with a US undergraduate sample. RESPONSE OPTIONS / INSTRUCTIONS: the paper (Materials, reproduced in the OSF Rmd l.138) states only the endpoints: 'We used a 1 (Dislike Strongly) to 7 (Like Strongly) Likert scale'; the export's sub-header row carries no scale-point labels. resp 1 and 7 text is therefore study-confirmed and matches the canonical form exactly; the labels for 2-6 ('Dislike Moderately','Dislike a Little','Neither like nor dislike','Like a Little','Like Moderately') and the instructions sentence are taken from the canonical STOMP-R form and were NOT confirmed as what the SurveyMonkey page displayed. Every item uses all 7 levels in the live data (min 1, max 7 per item). RIGHTS: Gosling lab STOMP page (sha256 809d3a72...ba776b) and Rentfrow's Cambridge measures page (sha256 7f89d98f...7b0a0003) both distribute the STOMP-R with no fee, permission, non-commercial or redistribution clause (0 matches for commercial/permission/copyright on the Gosling page); the items are 23 genre names. Silence -> extract; no register row written. RESPONSE DATA: live table has n~525-535 per item, above the paper's valid n=389, because the IRW table keeps respondents who failed the Catch1 attention check (the paper filters Catch1 == 1; IRW carries it as cov_catch1). Not an item-text issue.

note: CONVENTION FOR THE FIVE bfi_goldberg_1992_* SIBLINGS (reuse for _conscientiousness/_extraversion/_neuroticism/_openness_to_experience): source is openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/BIG5.zip (sha256 67953298d75d3279d0486e7f4ec0195efc26a9e790b15e511cbcf4551751ba53, fetched 2026-09-19), whose BIG5/codebook.txt keys every data.csv column E1..E10, N1..N10, A1..A10, C1..C10, O1..O10 to its verbatim statement (tab-separated, CRLF). data/bfi_goldberg_1992.r selects those columns BY NAME (A_items <- paste0('A',1:10)) and pivots names_to='item', so the IRW code IS the source column name -- no positional step, nothing inferred; mapping_basis=data_labels (codebook level, 10/10 codes matched). item_text copied verbatim from the codebook, including its leading 'I ' (this codebook, unlike the AS+SC+AD+DO one, prints the prefix itself) and final period. Anchors from the codebook sentence 'rated on a five point scale where 1=Disagree, 3=Neutral, 5=Agree (0=missed)': resp 1/3/5 labelled, resp 2 and 4 left blank (unlabelled, not padded). data.csv 0=missed is set to NA by the script, hence live resp set 1-5. instructions = first sentence of the Procedure paragraph of https://openpsychometrics.org/tests/IPIP-BFFM/ (page sha256 9c14b38a..., 'Updated: 2 August 2019'); the data were collected c.2012 (codebook), so this is the test's current landing-page wording, not a confirmed 2012 screen; the second sentence ('It takes most people 3-8 minutes to complete.') was omitted as not an instruction. STEP 3b: the dictionary Description says 'Big Five Inventory' and the table name says bfi, but the live items are NOT the BFI-44 (John et al.) -- they are the 50-item IPIP Big-Five Factor Markers (Goldberg 1992), confirmed word for word against ipip.ori.org/newBigFive5broadKey.htm Factor II 10-item scale (+ keyed: interested in people, sympathize, soft heart, take time out, feel others' emotions, make people feel at ease; - keyed: not really interested, insult, not interested in problems, little concern). instrument field names the IPIP markers accordingly. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv IPIP row, verdict ship (batch_140) applied, not re-derived; ipip.ori.org home page re-read 2026-09-19: 'The items and scales are in the public domain, which means that one can copy, edit, translate, or use them for any purpose without asking permission and without paying a fee.' The BFI-44 block row does not apply (different instrument). The test page's 'Your use of this tool should be for educational or entertainment purposes only ... no guarantee of accuracy or fitness' is a fitness disclaimer about the online tool, not a right reserved over the public-domain wording, so it does not block. Sanity (not required for data_labels): in the local data.csv the four codebook-negative items A1/A3/A5/A7 have means 2.31/2.16/2.17/2.16 vs 3.68-4.03 for the rest and correlate -0.15..-0.57 with A2, so the stored data are raw (unreversed) and the Disagree..Agree direction holds; live per-item n = 19718 for all 10 items (irw_table_sets) = local non-missing counts.
public_note: The dictionary calls this table the Big Five Inventory, but its items are the IPIP Big-Five Factor Markers (Goldberg, 1992) administered by the Open-Source Psychometrics Project, not the BFI-44.
